page: Microsoft Azure M32bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, but it is Premium Storage capable and optimized for block storage performance. No GPU accelerators are present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific processing tasks. The instance achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core performance with a score of 2210.0, and strong multi-core performance with a score of 18347.0. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 33.05 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs at 210.74 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 25 percent. Static web serving throughput is also strong at 53.69 GB/sec. For artificial intelligence workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds of 343.5 tokens/sec using a small 135M LLM model, though performance drops to a weak 2.74 tokens/sec when executing text generation on a large 70B model. Other metrics, such as Redis SET operations at 44.24 million operations per second and Passmark CPU scores, fall within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M32bs_v3 offers a high-density memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring substantial RAM without the overhead of excessive vCPU counts. The absence of local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale block storage independently. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including medium-sized databases, caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
